notes.backupPowerSource: A backup power source means a battery, auxiliary power unit (APU), ram air turbine (RAT), etc.
notes.displaysDefinition: A “display” means EFIS, ECAM, EICAS, PFD, ND, or similar.
notes.materialsAndLabor: Total repair cost includes estimated cost of materials and labor.

options.landingGear: Landing gear, wheels, brakes, or tires
options.propeller: Release of all or a portion of a propeller blade
options.taxiway: Takeoff or landing from a taxiway
options.wrongRunway: Takeoff or landing from an incorrect runway

questions.aircraftMajorDamage: Which parts of the aircraft received major damage?
questions.complianceNecessary: Was compliance with the resolution advisory necessary to avoid a potential collision?
questions.contained: Was the failure contained to within the engine?
questions.correctiveAction: Did another aircraft have to take immediate corrective action?
questions.degree: What was the most severe type of burns received?
questions.electricContinuous: Did you have to continually use an emergency bus powered by a backup power source?
questions.escapeSlidesUsed: Were any emergency egress systems (e.g., escape slides) used?
questions.fingerToeNose: Was only a finger bone, nose bone, or toe bone broken?
questions.fmvLessThan25Grand: Is the fair market value of the damaged property $25,000 or less?
questions.groundContactDamage: Was the damage caused by the blade contacting the ground?
questions.groundContactRelease: Was the release caused by the blade contacting the ground?
questions.hydraulicContinuous: Did you have to continually use the remaining hydraulic systems, or a mechanical system?
questions.lessThan25Grand: Is the total cost to repair the damage estimated at $25,000 or less?
questions.major: Would the damaged rotor blade require major repair or replacement?
questions.majorRepair: Would the damage require major repair or replacement?
questions.moreThan1EngineDamaged: Are two or more engines damaged?
questions.moreThan1EngineThrustLoss: Did the loss of thrust occur in more than one engine?
questions.moreThanHalf: Did more than half of your displays completely fail?
questions.over5Percent: Were these burns over more than 5% of the body?
questions.performNormalDuties: Was the crewmember still able to perform their normal duties?
questions.publicAirport: Did it happen at a public airport?
questions.requiredCrewmember: Was the person a required crewmember at the time of the illness or injury?
questions.severe: Was the hemorrhage classified as severe?
questions.simpleFracture: Was it a simple (not compound) fracture?
questions.twoDaysOrLonger: Did anyone stay in the hospital longer than 48 hours?
questions.within7Days: Was anyone hospitalized within 7 days of the incident?
questions.within30Days: Did death occur within 30 days of the incident?

subtitles.propertyDamage: Damage to property other than your aircraft.

welcome.title: Help! I crashed my plane!
welcome.description: Oh no! I’m here to help you figure out if you have to notify the NTSB, and when.
welcome.footer: This website was created by {me} during the COVID-19 shelter-in-place order of April 2020.

incident.title: Based on your answers, this qualifies as an {level}.
incident.actions: You are not required to notify the NTSB or file an accident report.

seriousIncident.title: Based on your answers, this qualifies as a {level}.
seriousIncident.actions: {notifyImmediately}. You do not have to file an accident report unless requested by the NTSB.
seriousIncident.notifyImmediately: You are required to notify the NTSB immediately

accident.title: Based on your answers, this qualifies as an {level}.
accident.actions: You are required to notify the NTSB immediately, and file an accident report.

immediateNotification.title: Immediate Notification
immediateNotification.description: You must immediately notify the nearest NTSB regional office of this incident.
immediateNotification.contact: Contact information for regional offices can be found at {URL}. You can also call the NTSB Response Operations Center at (844) 373-9922 or (202) 314-6290.
immediateNotification.whatToInclude: You should reference 49 CFR § 830.6 for what to include in your notification.

accidentReport.title: Accident Report
accidentReport.description: You are required to make a report of this accident to the NTSB within 10 days after the accident.
accidentReport.form: You must fill out {form6120} or 6120.2 (OMB No. 3147-0001). Send the completed form to the applicable address shown in  the form description.

finished.disclaimer: Important disclaimer: This website should not be used as a source for legal advice. Consult an aviation attorney.
finished.applicableRegulations: The regulations that apply to your incident are 49 CFR § {regulations}.
